```artifact
Feature: Doorstop Requirements Management

  Scenario: Store requirements securely - Normal Case
    Given a Doorstop instance is running
    When a user adds a requirement with ID "REQ-001" and text "This is a normal requirement."
    Then the requirement "REQ-001" is stored persistently
    And the requirement "REQ-001" is accessible with the correct text.

  Scenario: Store requirements securely - Edge Case: Long Requirement Text
    Given a Doorstop instance is running
    When a user adds a requirement with ID "REQ-002" and text with 2000 characters (as specified)
    Then the requirement "REQ-002" is stored persistently
    And the requirement "REQ-002" is accessible with the complete text.

  Scenario: Store requirements securely - Negative Case: Invalid Requirement ID
    Given a Doorstop instance is running
    When a user attempts to add a requirement with an invalid ID "REQ-!" and text "Invalid ID test"
    Then an error message "Invalid requirement ID format" is displayed
    And the requirement is not stored.

  Scenario Outline: Handle Requirement Changes - Normal and Edge Cases
    Given a Doorstop instance is running
    And a requirement with ID "<Requirement ID>" and text "<Original Text>" exists
    When a user changes the text of requirement "<Requirement ID>" to "<New Text>" with developer ID "DEV-001"
    Then the requirement "<Requirement ID>" is updated with the new text "<New Text>"
    And the change is associated with developer ID "DEV-001"

    Examples:
      | Requirement ID | Original Text | New Text |
      | REQ-001 | This is a normal requirement. | This is an updated normal requirement. |
      | REQ-003 | Short text. | Very long text with 1999 characters (as specified). |
      | REQ-004 | Initial text. |  | # Empty new text

  Scenario: Handle Requirement Changes - Negative Case: Attempt to Change Non-Existent Requirement
    Given a Doorstop instance is running
    When a user attempts to change the text of requirement "REQ-999" to "New Text" with developer ID "DEV-001"
    Then an error message "Requirement not found" is displayed
    And the requirement "REQ-999" does not exist.

  Scenario: Associate Changes with Developer - Normal Case
    Given a Doorstop instance is running
    And a requirement with ID "REQ-005" and text "Initial text" exists
    When a user changes the text of requirement "REQ-005" to "Updated text" with developer ID "DEV-002"
    Then the change history for requirement "REQ-005" includes an entry with developer ID "DEV-002".

  Scenario: Scalability - Support Thousands of Requirements
    Given a Doorstop instance is running
    When a user adds 1000 requirements with unique IDs "REQ-1000" to "REQ-1999" and arbitrary text (as specified)
    Then all 1000 requirements are stored persistently
    And all 1000 requirements are accessible.

  Scenario Outline: Scalability - Boundary Case: Maximum Requirements
    Given a Doorstop instance is running
    When a user adds requirements up to the maximum supported limit of <Number of Requirements>
    Then all requirements are stored persistently
    And all requirements are accessible

    Examples:
      | Number of Requirements |
      | 10000 |
      | 10001 |

  Scenario: Lightweight Installation - Successful Installation
    Given a Doorstop instance is not installed
    When a user executes the lightweight installation method
    Then Doorstop is installed successfully
    And Doorstop is running.
```
